The World Economic Outlook (WEO) database contains selected macroeconomic data series from the statistical appendix of the World Economic Outlook report, which presents the IMF staff's analysis and projections of economic developments at the global level, in major country groups and in many individual countries. The WEO is released in April and September/October each year.
Use this database to find data on national accounts, inflation, unemployment rates, balance of payments, fiscal indicators, trade for countries and country groups (aggregates), and commodity prices whose data are reported by the IMF.
Data are available from 1980 to the present, and projections are given for the next two years. Additionally, medium-term projections are available for selected indicators. For some countries, data are incomplete or unavailable for certain years.
The World Economic Outlook (WEO) database is now available in SDMX format from our Entire Dataset page. For more information about SDMX, please visit SDMX.org.
Changes to the October 2024 Database

    Following the recent release of the 2021 survey by the World Bank Group’s International Comparison Program for new purchasing-power-parity benchmarks, the WEO’s estimates of purchasing-power-parity weights and GDP valued at purchasing power parity have been updated. For more details, see Box A2.
    For Bangladesh, fiscal year estimates of real GDP and purchasing-power-parity GDP are now used in country group aggregates.
    For Montenegro, historical data prior to 2023 for population and GDP per capita are excluded from publication pending the final release of population estimates from the 2023 Census of Population, Households, and Dwellings.
    For Zimbabwe, the authorities have recently redenominated their national accounts statistics following the introduction on April 5, 2024 of a new national currency, the Zimbabwe gold, replacing the Zimbabwe dollar. The use of the Zimbabwe dollar ceased on April 30, 2024.

import numpy as np

# Treasury data (in millions of dollars)
# June 1991 (revised in Dec 1991 bulletin)
june_1991_europe = 267252
june_1991_latam = 336586

# June 1996 (revised in Dec 1996 bulletin)
june_1996_europe = 431266
june_1996_latam = 444900

print("=== Treasury Data (millions USD) ===")
print(f"June 1991 Europe: {june_1991_europe}")
print(f"June 1991 Latin America & Caribbean: {june_1991_latam}")
print(f"June 1996 Europe: {june_1996_europe}")
print(f"June 1996 Latin America & Caribbean: {june_1996_latam}")

# Germany GDP (World Bank data in current US$)
germany_gdp_1991 = 1875792575132.59
germany_gdp_1996 = 2506576553158.31

# Convert to billions and round to 2 decimal points
germany_gdp_1991_b = round(germany_gdp_1991 / 1e9, 2)
germany_gdp_1996_b = round(germany_gdp_1996 / 1e9, 2)

print(f"\n=== Germany Nominal GDP (World Bank) ===")
print(f"1991: ${germany_gdp_1991_b} billion")
print(f"1996: ${germany_gdp_1996_b} billion")

# Germany's percentage growth rate
germany_growth_rate = (germany_gdp_1996_b - germany_gdp_1991_b) / germany_gdp_1991_b * 100
print(f"Germany GDP growth rate: {germany_growth_rate:.4f}%")

# Counterfactual Europe = June 1991 Europe * (1 + Germany growth rate)
counterfactual_europe = june_1991_europe * (1 + germany_growth_rate/100)
print(f"\nCounterfactual Europe (June 1991 * Germany growth): {counterfactual_europe:.2f}")

# Linear regression with Europe as predictor of Latin America
# Using the two observed data points (1991 and 1996)
X = np.array([june_1991_europe, june_1996_europe])
y = np.array([june_1991_latam, june_1996_latam])

# Fit linear regression: y = slope * x + intercept
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(X, y, 1)
print(f"\n=== Linear Regression ===")
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f}")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.2f}")

# Predict Latin America using counterfactual Europe
predicted_latam = slope * counterfactual_europe + intercept
print(f"Predicted Latin America (counterfactual): {predicted_latam:.2f}")

# Actual June 1996 Latin America
actual_latam_1996 = june_1996_latam
print(f"Actual June 1996 Latin America: {actual_latam_1996}")

# Absolute difference
abs_diff = abs(predicted_latam - actual_latam_1996)
print(f"Absolute difference: {abs_diff:.2f}")

# Percentage of actual June 1996 value
pct_of_actual = (abs_diff / actual_latam_1996) * 100
print(f"Absolute difference as % of actual: {pct_of_actual:.4f}%")

# U.S. total liabilities growth ratio (using Europe + Latin America as proxy)
us_liabilities_1991 = june_1991_europe + june_1991_latam
us_liabilities_1996 = june_1996_europe + june_1996_latam
us_growth_ratio = us_liabilities_1996 / us_liabilities_1991
print(f"\n=== U.S. Liabilities Growth ===")
print(f"1991 (Europe+LatAm): {us_liabilities_1991}")
print(f"1996 (Europe+LatAm): {us_liabilities_1996}")
print(f"Growth ratio: {us_growth_ratio:.6f}")

# Germany GDP growth ratio
germany_gdp_ratio = germany_gdp_1996 / germany_gdp_1991
print(f"\nGermany GDP growth ratio: {germany_gdp_ratio:.6f}")

# Final answer
final_ratio = us_growth_ratio / germany_gdp_ratio
final_answer = pct_of_actual * final_ratio
print(f"\n=== Final Calculation ===")
print(f"Ratio of US growth to Germany GDP growth: {final_ratio:.6f}")
print(f"Final answer: {pct_of_actual:.4f} * {final_ratio:.6f} = {final_answer:.2f}")
print(f"\nFinal Answer (rounded to 2 decimal places): {final_answer:.2f}")
